answer: Extracted scientific evidence from 'Influence of El Niño southern oscillation on precipitation variability in Northeast Thailand' (Chueasa et al., 2024, MethodsX 13, 102954).

paper_metadata.title: Influence of El Niño southern oscillation on precipitation variability in Northeast Thailand
author_affiliations: Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, King Mongkut’s University of Technology Thonburi (KMUTT), Bangkok, Thailand
The Joint Graduate School of Energy and Environment (JGSEE), King Mongkut’s University of Technology Thonburi (KMUTT), Bangkok, Thailand

study_region.name: Northeast Thailand (Isan / Korat Plateau)
study_region.topography: Plateau landscape bounded by Mekong River (North/East) and Phetchabun Mountains (West)

missing_data_imputation.imputation_process: Missing daily/monthly precipitation records were estimated using linear regression models built from surrounding neighboring stations

section_2_ssta_regions_and_oceanic_indic.ssta_data_source: NOAA Extended Reconstructed Sea Surface Temperature version 5 (ERSST.v5)

analyzed_nino_regions.description: Easternmost and smallest equatorial Pacific region off coastal South America; exhibits highest SSTA variance
Eastern equatorial Pacific region key for ocean-atmosphere interaction monitoring
Central equatorial Pacific region representing average equatorial Pacific SSTA
Central-western equatorial Pacific region capturing maximum warm SSTA pool

section_3_quantitative_lag_time_response.lag_response_summary: Precipitation anomaly (PPTA) response to ENSO SSTA exhibits a 4–5 month lag period across Northeast Thailand
section_3_quantitative_lag_time_response.wave_propagation_mechanism: The 4–5 month delay is governed by the slow propagation of oceanic Kelvin and Rossby waves across the equatorial Pacific, which takes several months to modulate atmospheric Walker Circulation and alter monsoon moisture delivery to Indochina

weak_and_moderate_correlations.el_nino_events: -0.01 to -0.32 across weak, moderate, and strong phases
weak_and_moderate_correlations.weak_moderate_la_nina: 0.01 to 0.29 across weak and moderate phases

physical_mechanisms_for_asymmetry.central_pacific_regions_nino_3_34_4: During Strong La Niña (SSTA < -1.5°C), enhanced trade winds and strengthened Walker Circulation shift deep atmospheric convection westward into Southeast Asia, driving sharp rainfall increases across Northeast Thailand
physical_mechanisms_for_asymmetry.coastal_region_nino_1_2_positive_correla: Localized oceanic-atmospheric feedbacks near coastal South America cause reduced cooling or localized warming during Strong La Niña, producing a local weakening of the eastern Walker Circulation branch that results in a positive correlation (+0.76) with Northeast Thailand rainfall

seasonal_distribution.rainy_season: Mid-May to mid-October (peaking in July, August, and September)
seasonal_distribution.dry_season: November to April (minimum rainfall in December and January)

section_6_wavelet_transform_coherence_wt.mother_wavelet: Morlet wavelet (central frequency omega_0 = 6 radians/unit time)

identified_periodicities.description: Dominant interannual coherence mode matching the 2–7 year primary cycle of ENSO recurrence, with highest power during 1993–2003 and 2013–2018
High intra-annual coherence during 2003–2013 reflecting semi-annual to annual seasonal modulations driven by ENSO

section_7_policy_and_water_management_re.early_warning_window: 4–5 months lead time based on Pacific SSTA index monitoring

recommendations_for_dcce_and_rid: Incorporate the 4–5 month early warning window into the Royal Irrigation Department (RID) seasonal water allocation and reservoir management models.
Issue advance agricultural notices 4–5 months prior to crop planting to guide rice, rubber, and sugarcane farmers on cropping choices and irrigation schedules.
Establish proactive flood retention and drainage management protocols in advance of Strong La Niña phases to handle precipitation surpluses of up to +34.13%.
Implement dry-season drought contingency planning, water rationing, and forest fire suppression measures 4 months ahead of El Niño onset.
